proposed_fixes.title: Keep final snapped geometry within the intended right-edge bounds
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: Edge's vertical-tab mode changes its minimum tracking size or effective frame geometry, and the final size accepted by the app differs from FancyZones' requested zone rectangle. DPI/frame conversion is an alternative that must be measured rather than presumed.
plan: Reproduce the same right-edge zone in Edge vertical and horizontal tab modes; record zone bounds, requested placement, final GetWindowRect/DWM visible bounds and minimum accepted width.

Inspect src/modules/fancyzones/FancyZonesLib/WindowUtils.cpp placement/border adjustment and the WorkArea placement caller to determine whether the application expands the window or FancyZones computes a wrong rectangle.

If placement ignores a confirmed application size constraint, anchor the final supported size to the appropriate work-area edge using existing placement policy; if frame conversion is wrong, correct only that conversion. Do not repeatedly force the app below its minimum size.
Add focused geometry tests for narrow right-edge zones, constrained windows and scaled displays, preserving unconstrained window placement.
verification: Switch Edge tab mode without changing the layout and compare the same snap operation.
Widen the zone beyond Edge's minimum width and confirm whether overflow disappears.
Test non-Edge windows, multiple DPI values and left/right work-area boundaries; ensure the correction does not introduce resize loops.

reproduce.title: FancyZones right-edge overflow with Edge vertical tabs
reproduce.version_requirement: Current PowerToys and Edge; compare the original 0.83.0 behavior only if needed.
prerequisites: A custom narrow zone touching the right work-area edge.
Edge with vertical and horizontal tab modes available; record DPI and monitor work area.
steps: Snap Edge with horizontal tabs into the right-edge zone and record its requested and actual visible bounds.
Enable vertical tabs and repeat with the identical layout and window state.
Manually find the smallest accepted Edge width and widen the zone above that width.
Compare GetWindowRect and DWM visible bounds against the zone and work area; identify whether the second size came from the app or placement code.
Repeat at another DPI and with an unconstrained ordinary window before selecting the geometry correction.
reproduce.expected_result: Snapping should honor established work-area placement policy and application size constraints without unexplained off-screen overflow or an endless resize fight.
